title: Gel and acrylic product safety, ventilation and mobile setup
audience: Mobile nail technicians who use gel, dip powder or acrylic products and lamps in a client's home or other location
learningOutcomes: Read a product safety data sheet and state the controls it sets for handling and storage
Set up a mobile station with adequate ventilation, power and a safe lamp position
Identify the warning signs that a client or technician is reacting to a product

instruction.heading: Reading the safety data sheet
instruction.body: Each gel, primer, dip powder, acrylic liquid and remover has a safety data sheet. The sheet sets out the hazards, the handling and storage controls, the first aid steps and the disposal method. Keep a current copy of each product on hand at the visit, and read it before first use. Some products are flagged for skin sensitisation. Product changes can change the hazards, so the sheet is checked when the product is changed.

instruction.heading: Ventilation and the work area
instruction.body: Acrylic liquid and monomer vapours and dust from filing can build up in a closed room. Open a window or use a fan that moves air away from the client and the technician, where the venue allows. Keep lids closed when not in use. A bathroom or small room with no airflow is not a suitable work area for acrylic work. UNCONFIRMED: no official source has been fetched for this point in this draft. A reviewer must confirm it before approval.

instruction.heading: Lamps and power
instruction.body: UV and LED lamps are plugged into a power point that is safe for the load, with the cord away from water and foot traffic. Check the lamp for damage before each visit. Keep the lamp on a stable surface. Set the timer the lamp manufacturer specifies. A lamp that is damaged or overheating is not used.

procedure: Check the safety data sheet for each product before the visit and keep a copy on hand
Check the power point, lamp and cord before setting up
Open ventilation or set up a fan that moves air away from the client, where the venue allows
Keep product lids closed and store products as the sheet directs between applications
Stop the service and tell the client if they report burning, swelling, redness or itching on the skin, and record the reaction

workedExamples.situation: A technician arrives at a client home for acrylic nails. The only room is a small bathroom with no window, and the client asks for the service there because it is the only room with a power point near a mirror.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Should the technician set up in the bathroom?
workedExamples.reasoning: The bathroom has no airflow and is a poor work area for acrylic vapours and dust. The technician asks for a room with a window or a fan option, and if none is possible, records that the service area is unsuitable and declines the acrylic part of the booking.

equipmentAndPpe: Safety data sheet for each product in use, on hand
Lamp with a current electrical test tag, where the business uses one
Closed storage for products between applications
Gloves suitable for the products used

commonErrors.error: Working in a closed room with no airflow.
commonErrors.prevention: Choose a room with ventilation or a fan. Decline acrylic work where that is not possible.

commonErrors.error: Using a damaged lamp or a damaged cord.
commonErrors.prevention: Check the lamp and cord before each visit and remove faulty equipment.

commonErrors.error: Continuing after a client reports skin reaction.
commonErrors.prevention: Stop, record the reaction and let the client remove the product before seeing a health professional.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Safety data sheets set the handling, storage and first aid controls for each product. The sheet is the reference, not this lesson.

Product sensitisation risks, ventilation standards and electrical testing rules vary by business and location. UNCONFIRMED: no official source has been fetched for this point in this draft. A reviewer must confirm it before approval.

qualityStandard: Every product in use has a current safety data sheet on hand
The work area has been checked for ventilation and power before the service
Any skin reaction is stopped and recorded
documentationEvidence: Product register with safety data sheet reference
Visit record of the work area and ventilation used
Record of any reaction and action taken
summary: Safety data sheets set the controls for each product
Acrylic work needs air movement and a suitable work area
Damaged equipment and skin reactions stop the service

knowledgeChecks.question: What should a technician read before using a new acrylic liquid?
options: The safety data sheet for that product

knowledgeChecks.question: A client reports burning and redness on the skin during a gel service. What is the correct action?
options: Keep going and apply a thicker layer
Stop, record the reaction and help the client remove the product
Ask the client to wait until the next visit

knowledgeChecks.question: Why is a closed bathroom a poor work area for acrylic work?
options: It is too warm for the lamp
Vapour and dust can build up with no airflow
